summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would make small changes to the Customs Tariff Act 1995.
It would remove Schedule 1 from the Act and let its content be set by regulations instead, and would repeal an expired safeguard provision for certain Thai imports.
The Enhanced Project By-law Scheme would be closed to new applicants, with the last active determination expiring by 31 December 2017.
changes: Repeals Schedule 1 of the Customs Tariff Act 1995, allowing country lists for preferential duty rates to be updated more easily through regulations.
Repeals section 16A, which contained expired safeguard provisions for tuna and pineapple products from Thailand.
Inserts new Additional Notes into Chapters 7, 8 and 19 of Schedule 3 to correct the classification of preserved fruits, vegetables and certain pastas.
Amends item 44 of Schedule 4 to set an end date of 31 December 2017 for the Enhanced Project By-law Scheme.
summary.affected: Importers of goods from countries listed in Schedule 1, importers of certain tuna and pineapple products from Thailand, and applicants to the Enhanced Project By-law Scheme would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The Customs Tariff Amendment Bill 2016 proposes four changes: moving preferential rate details to regulations for faster updates; removing expired Thailand-Australia Free Trade Agreement safeguards; adding tariff classification notes for fruits, vegetables and pastas following tribunal decisions; and closing the Enhanced Project By-law Scheme to new applicants by 31 December 2017.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Customs Tariff Amendment Bill 2016, which repeals schedule 1 and section 16A of the Customs Tariff Act, adds classification notes for fruits, vegetables and pasta, and amends item 44 for an end date, projecting $220 million in additional revenue. The bill clarifies tariff classification for gherkins and seafood won tons following Administrative Appeals Tribunal decisions.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: The Customs Tariff Amendment Bill 2016 includes four amendments to the Customs Act 1901, the first of which repeals schedule 1 of the act and relocates it to the Customs Tariff Regulations 2004.
